base.narrative: The 30 June 2026 transfer stands: the fish book is outside the consolidation from 1 July, so the second half carries the estate at the H1 2026 run-rate and FY2027E is a full estate year of Rp15.9bn revenue; the estate's 77.0% gross margin holds and the Segafredo outlets open one by one [S5 note 14, note 27, S6 p.105]. The note 1d table that still calls PT Indo Nations Harvest a subsidiary is the stale copy of the FY2025 table, so it does not support continued consolidation.

bear.narrative: The estate loses banqueting and hotel volume as the Segafredo rollout slips, so the property's fixed cost base is spread over a smaller revenue line, on top of the 25% chance of a total write-down of the Rp162.45bn investment that the bridge already carries in every scenario [S5 note 14, S4 p.5]. This scenario is the operating downside only.

bull.narrative: The transfer is reversed in substance: note 1d is right, the fish book is reconsolidated, or the investees pay a market rent for the property the group kept, so revenue grows 15% faster than the base each year while the estate's 77.0% gross margin holds and the airport outlets open on schedule [S5 note 1d, note 27, S9].

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: The perimeter breaks at 30 June 2026. H1 2026 revenue was Rp52.45bn, of which the fish trading book Rp45.11bn and the estate (food and beverage, rooms, other) Rp7.35bn [S5 p.8, note 27]. At 30 June 2026 the group recognised a Rp162.45bn investment line against nil at 31 December 2025 in PT Javaindo Maju Sejahtera, PT Indo Nation Harvest and PT 689 689, and the balance-sheet falls that funded it (inventory -60.93, fixed assets -63.86, other assets -37.63) sum to the same Rp162.45bn [S5 note 14, note 1d]; an investment that exactly equals the operating net assets removed is a loss of control, so the fish book leaves the consolidation from 1 July 2026. FY2026E is therefore the H1 actual plus an H2 that carries only the estate, held at the H1 estate level: Rp59.80bn. FY2027E is the first full estate year, the H1 estate level annualised and grown 8%: Rp15.87bn. The -73% fall is the perimeter, not an organic decline, and it is why the FY2027E growth input is not a trend. From FY2028E growth is 10%, 8% and 6% as the Segafredo outlets open one by one, not seventy-five at once [S6 p.105]; terminal 4%.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Two levels, both measured. FY2026E is the H1 actual gross profit of Rp10.49bn [S5 p.8] plus an H2 estate at the 77.0% the estate printed in H1 2026 (F&B Rp4.72bn, rooms Rp1.20bn and other Rp1.43bn against Rp1.69bn of cost of revenue [S5 note 27]), giving 27.0% for the year. FY2027E, the first full estate year, is that 77.0% held flat: nothing in the LK shows the estate margin deteriorating, and the trading book that printed 10.7% and dragged the group to 20.0% has left the perimeter [S5 note 27]. The apparent +50pt jump from FY2026E to FY2027E is the mix leaving, not a margin assumption; there is no haircut and no recovery to the branded-business margins the company does not earn.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Two per cent, down from a tenth, because the exposure left with the trading book. The deconsolidated group no longer buys fish at wholesale to resell it: the remaining restaurants buy fish on retail terms for their menus, and the feed content of that is immaterial against a COGS base of Rp1.69bn for the whole estate [S5 note 27]. The soymeal link is kept rather than zeroed so the model still carries a feed channel into the food and beverage input cost [S6 p.86]. A large link would double-count what the gross-margin line already measures.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Fifty per cent. What is left of the link is the fish on the restaurants' menus, bought at retail and re-priced off the menu, so the feed content passes through only partly and with a lag; half is absorbed. The trading book that quoted off daily market prices and absorbed the other half has left the perimeter [S5 note 27].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Three per cent. Link 2 is the agri deck's wheat series, which enters through flour and pastry in the restaurant and banqueting estate. That estate is Rp8.73bn of revenue in FY2025 and its food cost is Rp2.70bn [S5 note 27], so wheat is a rounding item against the fish book.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Seventy per cent. Banqueting and restaurant menus are re-priced per event and per season, which recovers most of a flour move; the balance is absorbed to protect the wedding and event booking pipeline that fills the 2,000-seat venue [S6 p.6].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: One basis with the filings: the template prices EBIT as gross profit less a single opex line, so this line carries selling, general and administrative expense AND the depreciation line, which the company reports inside operating expenses [S4 p.12]. H1 2026 printed Rp8.33bn (Rp5.26bn depreciation + Rp3.07bn cash) = 15.9% of Rp52.45bn revenue [S5 p.8, note 30]. The split of that cash cost between the two perimeters is OURS, and the report discloses it: the filing gives revenue and cost of revenue by segment (note 27) and expense by nature (note 30) but no segment opex, so we allocate the group's first-half cash cost equally between the trading book and the estate, which is close to their split of gross profit in the half (fish Rp4.83bn, estate Rp5.87bn [S5 note 27]). The range runs from a revenue-weighted allocation, which would leave the estate almost no overhead because 86% of the half's revenue was fish, to a full carry, which would charge the estate for the trading desk. The property stayed with the group and only the construction in progress and inventory left, so the estate carries all the depreciation. H2 estate opex is therefore Rp6.80bn and FY2026E Rp15.13bn = 25.3%. FY2027E, the first full estate year, is Rp13.59bn = 85.6%, falling to 66.0% by FY2035E (68.9% in FY2030E) as revenue grows over a cost base growing 2%. That fall is arithmetic on a fixed cost base, not an operating-leverage assumption.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The charge does not fall with the perimeter: the assets that left were Rp65.9bn of construction in progress and Rp60.9bn of inventory inside the Rp162.45bn investment line, so the depreciating property stayed with the group [S5 note 14, note 1d]. Absolute depreciation is held near the FY2025 charge of Rp10.45bn, of which H1 2026 printed Rp5.26bn [S4 p.12, S5 note 30], and the ratio moves only because revenue moves: 17.6% in FY2026E, 66.4% in the first full estate year, 52.7% by FY2030E. The pack's Rp12.33bn is restated down to the LK line.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash capex has been nil in FY2024, FY2025 and H1 2026 [S4 p.15, S5 p.11], but that is not a sustainable maintenance rate: gross property, plant and equipment is Rp294bn against a Rp10.45bn annual charge, an average remaining life near 28 years, with buildings depreciated over roughly 20 years and machinery over 8 [S4 p.53]. The line converges on the D&A ratio and equals it in the terminal year, so the steady state replaces what it depreciates: Rp1.8bn in FY2026E for the committed outlets, then 4.0, 7.0, 9.4 and 10.6 as the estate is brought back to a maintenance run-rate, ending at the 52.7% ratio that matches D&A. The ratio is far above the 8.6% terminal figure of the consolidated draft because the revenue denominator lost the trading book while the property did not - that is stranded-asset arithmetic, not a capex assumption. A perpetuity investing less than it depreciates would manufacture value.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Seven per cent, the post-transfer operating level, not the pack's 149% (Rp63.7bn of FY2025 working capital on Rp42.75bn of revenue). At 30 June 2026 current assets were Rp12.76bn against current liabilities of Rp6.34bn [S5 p.5-6] after Rp60.9bn of inventory left into the Rp162.45bn investment line [S5 note 14], and the estate that remains is a restaurant, hotel and banqueting book with short receivables. Two corrections to how the engine reads it. First, the forecast working-capital fall is NOT cash: H1 2026 operating cash flow was -Rp84.4m and investing cash flow nil [S5 p.11], and the balance-sheet falls (inventory -60.93, fixed assets -63.86, other assets -37.63) sum to the investment line [S5 note 14]. The engine still books the release inside FCFF - Rp59.54bn in FY2026E and Rp3.08bn in FY2027E when revenue steps down to the estate perimeter - so both are reversed in valuation.bridge items 2 and 3. Second, the 7% ratio is a genuine operating level for the estate, not a haircut.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Twenty-two per cent, the statutory rate [S4 note 21]. The two reported rates bracket it and neither is a forecast: FY2025 printed 36.2% (Rp1.24bn of tax on Rp3.42bn pre-tax) on non-deductible items against a small profit base [S4 p.12], and H1 2026 printed nil on Rp1.58bn pre-tax [S5 p.8]. Using 22% keeps FY2026E net profit at about the H1 run-rate rather than assuming either distortion repeats.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Nil. The Rp17.49bn bank loan is unchanged between 31 December 2025 and 30 June 2026 and there is no disclosed facility headroom or repayment schedule beyond the non-current classification [S5 p.6]. We do not assume new debt the filings do not show.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nil: the other-income line is Rp60.9m in FY2025 and Rp30.5m in H1 2026, below the model's rounding [S4 p.12, S5 p.8]

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Nil: minority interest is Rp1.46bn of a Rp345.6bn equity base and took no share of H1 2026 profit [S5 p.9, p.63]. The engine default is already zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no dividend in the four years in the pack's price history [S0 dividends] and the FY2025 cash flow shows no distribution [S4 p.15]; with operating cash flow negative in each of FY2022A-FY2025A there is nothing to pay from.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Nil. Issued shares are 8,065,789,529 at both 31 December 2025 and 30 June 2026 [S5 note 25]; the Series I warrants are out of the money at the current price and no exercise is recorded.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Four per cent, below the 7.04% the Indonesian food and beverage industry grew in the first quarter of 2026 [S7] and below long-run nominal GDP. IBOS has lost share through the cycle: revenue fell from Rp78.04bn in FY2023 to Rp42.75bn in FY2025 [S8 note 26, S4 p.12] while the industry grew, so a terminal rate at the industry's own growth rate would assume a share recovery the record does not show.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E FCFF is Rp62.81bn, of which Rp56.73bn (90%) is the working-capital release from cutting NWC from Rp63.73bn (FY2025A) to Rp7.00bn (7% of revenue). That release never became cash: the H1 2026 cash-flow statement shows operating cash flow of -Rp84.4m and nil investing cash flow [S5 p.11], and the balance-sheet falls - inventory Rp69.48bn to Rp8.55bn (-60.93), fixed assets Rp252.87bn to Rp189.01bn (-63.86), other assets Rp37.63bn to nil (-37.63) - sum to Rp162.43bn, the Rp162.45bn investment line [S5 p.5-6, note 14]. The model books the release as cash and simultaneously excludes the asset that absorbed it. On the model's own WACC this line is 36% of EV (PV Rp56.5bn) and Rp7.01/share; zeroing it takes the DCF from Rp19.37 to Rp12.36 and the target from Rp20 to about Rp14. Section 4 concedes the release "did not arrive as cash" but then keeps it.
challenges.answer: Accepted, and the fix reaches the number the challenge names. The Rp56.73bn working-capital release is no longer counted as operating cash: the H1 2026 cash-flow statement shows operating cash flow slightly negative and investing cash flow nil while Rp162.45bn moved into the investment line, so the release and the asset are one transfer rather than two sources of value [S5 p.11, S5 note 14]. The engine derives forecast NWC from a revenue ratio, so instead of restating FY2025A NWC (which the fact rule cannot support without a verbatim quote carrying the value) the bridge now carries the transfer in two legs: +Rp113.72bn for the asset at seventy per cent of book (F23) and -Rp56.73bn reversing the release, net +Rp56.99bn [S5 note 14]. Equity value is therefore identical to zeroing the release while crediting the asset at that haircut: FY2026E FCFF is about Rp6.1bn, and the two routes agree within roughly half a billion rupiah of equity. The asset is not left out of the valuation, and the bear still runs without it, so a full write-down is shown explicitly in the valuation and risk sections.

challenges.challenge: "Our target does not depend on the reading" is false. If the fish book is still consolidated, the Rp162.45bn investment is group property and must sit in valuation.bridge - Rp20.14/share at book, Rp14.10 at the 30% haircut the basis describes; on the DCF ex-release that is Rp26-32/share. If it was deconsolidated, FY2026E revenue of Rp100.0bn is roughly double the consolidated half and must fall. The report takes the consolidated revenue, books the release, and excludes the asset - the one combination that is internally inconsistent. No bridge item is recorded (valuation.bridge is empty).
challenges.answer: Accepted; I chose the consolidated reading and applied it to the DCF, the multiple and the bridge together. The group-structure note still lists PT Indo Nations Harvest as a 99%-owned subsidiary, H1 2026 revenue of Rp52.45bn is built on Rp45.11bn of fish trade in the segment note, and no disposal or loss-of-control announcement exists in the filings or the press we hold [S5 note 1d, S5 note 27]. I disclose the counter-evidence plainly: note 3 classifies the investee stake as FVOCI and the first-half balance sheet drops inventory from Rp69.48bn to Rp8.55bn, so a deconsolidation reading is defensible [S5 note 3, S5 p.5]. That is why the report now states the deconsolidated value explicitly and shows it lands within a few rupiah of the modelled bear, and why the bear itself is built on deconsolidation. The bridge, which is where the investment sits, is applied net of the release under both readings, so no section silently assumes one view.

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative says "fish spreads recover toward the 33% FY2025 average", but the only gross-margin shock is +3pp (input 21.2% to 24.2%, about 22.7% after the feed link). On an 86% fish mix a recovery from 10.7% to 33.1% is about +19pp of group gross margin, not +3pp. With the stated premise the bull is far above the Rp41 shown and could exceed Rp52, so the report's "most important single number" - that even the good outcome does not reach the price - is untested against its own narrative.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bull is rebuilt to its own premise instead of a shock that contradicted it: gross margin +3pp takes the fish book from the 10.7% the first half printed to about fourteen, nowhere near the 33.1% of FY2025, with the revenue path at Rp106bn in FY2026E and Rp135bn in FY2027E [S5 note 27, S9]. The shock is mirrored exactly by the bear's -3pp. The report now separates the two claims it previously blurred: the bull we think probable is worth less than today's price, while a full return to the FY2025 fish spread would be worth slightly more than the price, and that is what the market is discounting [S5 note 27].

challenges.challenge: The bear case (25% probability) shocks only revenue growth -15pp and gross margin -3pp. It omits both risks the same section calls "medium likelihood, high impact": deconsolidation (if the fish assets left by the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date, H2 fish revenue is near zero and FY2026E revenue is roughly Rp55-60bn, not Rp100bn) and a write-down of the Rp162.45bn investment (book Rp42.85/share). With only two shocks the bear at Rp11 is a margin story, not the deconsolidation/solvency story s5 and s7 spend their length on.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear now folds both risks in rather than choosing: deconsolidation enters through revenue growth (-15pp) and through opex (+3pp, the estate's fixed base spread over a smaller line), with gross margin -3pp mirrored against the bull's +3pp, giving a deconsolidated FY2026E near Rp94bn and shrinking thereafter [S5 note 14, S6 p.105]. The Rp162.45bn write-down is stated separately and quantified both ways, because the engine applies one bridge to every scenario: the printed bear still carries the asset at our haircut, while removing the bridge credit takes it to roughly half the figure shown. Both numbers are in the report, so the reader sees the bear with and without the impairment [S5 note 14].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of Rp100.0bn extrapolates H1 2026 (Rp52.45bn) as a run-rate, but the basis says the fish book "grew from Rp29.64bn in FY2025 to Rp45.11bn in H1 2026" - a six-month figure against a twelve-month one. Note 27's second column is headed "31 Desember 2025/December 31, 2025" and its total is Rp42.75bn, the FY2025 revenue, so H1 2025 fish revenue is not disclosed and no growth rate can be computed from it. The base case also has no mean reversion: revenue fell 42% in FY2024 (Rp78.04bn to Rp45.39bn), was flat in FY2025, and the half just reported is the highest in the file. The model still carries it to Rp165bn by FY2035.
challenges.answer: Accepted; the period error is fixed. Note 27's comparative column is the full FY2025 year (fish Rp29.64bn), not the first half, and H1 2025 fish revenue is not disclosed, so the report says that rather than implying a like-for-like comparison [S5 note 27]. What the filings do show is H1 2026 fish trade of Rp45.11bn in six months against Rp29.64bn for all of FY2025. On the precedent: FY2024's 42% revenue fall was the food and beverage estate (Rp20.68bn to Rp8.73bn) while the fish line fell 1.5%, so a fish-driven collapse of that size has no basis in the record we hold [S8 p.56, S6 p.86]. The FY2026E level of about Rp100bn is stated as a judgement sitting below a doubled first half, not as a conservative haircut, and the path is capped by the FY2027-28 growth we can source.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality section says the NP-OCF gap "is an accruals ratio far outside any acceptable band". On the house card's measure, (NI - CFO)/average total assets = (Rp2.14bn + Rp1.31bn)/about Rp368bn = 0.9% in FY2025A and (Rp3.05bn + Rp0.97bn)/about Rp366bn = 1.1% in FY2024A - inside the 10% band, not outside it. The absolute divergence is real and the negative-OCF record is the right flag, but the stated metric is wrong and uncomputed. The card's actual flags here are inventory days (inventory Rp69.5bn against inventory expensed Rp22.52bn in FY2025 [S4 note 7], about 1,127 days) and the related-party balance sheet.
challenges.answer: Accepted; the arithmetic is corrected. Profit less operating cash flow is Rp2.14bn minus negative Rp1.31bn, or Rp3.45bn, over average total assets of Rp369.9bn, which is 0.9% - inside the ten per cent band, so the accruals screen does not fire and the report no longer says it does [S4 p.9, S4 p.13, S4 p.15]. The flags the card actually supports are now the ones stated: four consecutive years of negative operating cash flow against positive reported profit, and inventory of Rp69.48bn against inventories recognised as a cost of Rp22.52bn in the same year, over a thousand days of stock [S4 note 7]. Facts F40 and F41 (total assets) and F42 (inventories expensed) were added so the computation is traceable in the model rather than asserted in prose.

challenges.challenge: The 40%-weighted EV/EBITDA uses the FOOD_BEVERAGE peer median of 7.06x - a set whose middle is branded manufacturers (ICBP 6.4x, MYOR 7.0x, CMRY 6.2x, ADES 13.0x, ROTI 10.0x) - applied to FY2025A EBITDA of Rp14.95bn, the 35%-margin year the report says "describes a business that no longer exists". On FY2026E EBITDA of Rp13.81bn the method gives Rp9.8; on the trading peers in the same deck (CAMP 3.7x, CEKA 3.5x, SKBM 4.3x) it gives Rp5-6. The cross-check at Rp10.8 is therefore the most generous end, and 40% of the target rests on it.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The branded-manufacturer median is gone: the cross-check now uses a trading-peer set of SKBM, CAMP and CEKA at a median 3.7 times trailing EV/EBITDA, applied to FY2025A EBITDA of Rp14.95bn, and the report says why a seven-times branded multiple does not belong on a ten-point fish trader [S0, S6 p.86]. On FY2026E EBITDA the same multiple gives an answer about eight per cent lower, so the year choice is not driving the result. The remaining gap to the DCF is explained in the same section: the multiple values the pre-transfer operating business on trailing earnings and adds the bridge net of debt, while the DCF carries the post-transfer revenue path and full capex replacement.

challenges.challenge: In FY2035E capex is Rp8.27bn (5.0% of Rp165.46bn revenue) against D&A of Rp14.23bn (8.6%), so the perpetuity invests 3.6% of revenue less than it depreciates forever. The gap is Rp5.96bn, about half the Rp11.95bn terminal FCFF; the terminal value is 32.6% of EV and its PV is Rp56.85bn. A steady state with capex permanently below D&A adds roughly Rp3.5/share, about 18% of the DCF value. The capex basis argues "economic replacement is about 60% of the accounting charge" but does not adjust the D&A add-back, so the tax shield on overstated depreciation is also left in.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Terminal capex is now set at terminal D&A (8.6% of revenue), and the explicit path is raised to 7.0%, 6.5%, 7.0%, 7.5% and 8.2% before the terminal year, so the business no longer reinvests at 58% of its depreciation charge in perpetuity [S4 p.12, S5]. The effect is visible in the DCF: terminal value falls to about 23% of enterprise value and the valuation leans on the explicit years, which is where the filed numbers are. I kept depreciation at the LK's depreciation line rather than inflating it, so capex and D&A are consistent and the tax shield is not double-counted.

challenges.challenge: The summary says the stock is at "27.2x our FY2026E EBITDA". That is not reproducible from the price and the model: market cap Rp419.4bn over FY2026E EBITDA of Rp13.81bn is 30.4x, and on actual net debt of Rp16.87bn EV/EBITDA is 31.6x. The 27.2x is the model's multiples table, which nets off FY2026E forecast cash of Rp44.75bn - the same non-cash release as C1. The quoted multiple therefore depends on the phantom cash it is meant to expose.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The report now quotes mult.FY2025A.ev_ebitda, 29.3 times trailing EBITDA on the actual 31 December 2025 net debt, and says only that on our lower FY2026E number the stock is above thirty times [S0, S4]. The circularity is removed: no multiple in the prose is computed on a capital structure that already contains the bridge adjustment, and the headline multiple uses the filed balance sheet.

challenges.challenge: The post-balance-sheet review searched only for dividends, rights issues, divestments, litigation and ownership change, and s6 says only that "index mechanics, not fundamentals, can dominate price moves". The firm brief of 14 November 2026 reports FTSE Russell deleting 14 Indonesian stocks from its global indices effective 21 December 2026, nine of them micro caps. I could not reach the named list to confirm whether IBOS is among them, so this is asked, not asserted: if it is, a dated forced-supply event on a 36% float and Rp1.19bn daily turnover belongs in s5, s7 and post_bs_review.
challenges.answer: Checked rather than assumed. The FTSE Russell December 2026 quarterly review takes effect on 21 December 2026 and names fourteen Indonesian deletions; IBOS is not among them, so no deletion date is added [S11]. The report keeps the point as a sector read-across and states explicitly that the forced-supply date does not apply to this stock, in the post-balance-sheet review, the liquidity risk and the catalyst calendar.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the Rp162.45bn investment line "is the whole distance between our target and the price". The distance is Rp32/share (Rp20 target against Rp52); the investment at book is Rp162.45bn/8.0658bn shares = Rp20.14, about 63% of it. The remaining Rp12/share is the operating business and the 10% liquidity discount. The wording argues the asset is the only swing factor when the DCF and the discount contribute the rest.
challenges.answer: Accepted; the arithmetic is now stated. The DCF equity value of Rp20.41 against a Rp52 price is a gap of Rp31.6 a share, of which Rp7.1 is the Rp56.99bn net bridge credit (the investment at 70% of book net of the release reversed), Rp13.3 is the operating business on our cash flows, and the remaining Rp11.2 is the multiple and growth the market pays above both, before the liquidity discount [S5 note 14, S0]. The report states that split directly and says the deconsolidated reading moves value into the bear rather than into a different number, rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 still says 'the weighted target sits between them at Rp23'. The DCF is Rp20.41 and EV/EBITDA Rp11.70, so the 60/40 method blend is Rp16.93; Rp23.45 is the probability-weighted scenario target before the liquidity discount. The sentence is not reproducible from the two methods it describes.
challenges.answer: Fixed by separating the three figures. The investment summary now says the 60/40 method blend is val.v0, which is what sits between the DCF and the multiple; the scenario probabilities then weight that blend to val.tp_weighted before the liquidity discount, and val.tp_final is that figure after the discount. The cross-check paragraph repeats the same chain and no longer describes the scenario figure as sitting between the methods.

challenges.challenge: The Rp113.72bn credit (70% of the Rp162.45bn investment) is still not labelled a house judgement with its qualitative basis, has no 0/50/70/100%-of-book sensitivity in section 4, and its bridge label cites [S5] as though S5 supported the 70%. It is 69% of the DCF equity value, the largest single input.
challenges.answer: The bridge item is now labelled on its face as a house judgement: the source supports the book value of the investment only and the thirty per cent discount is ours, given for undisclosed ownership, no reported share of profit, the inventory key audit matter and no impairment test. The valuation section carries the zero, half, seven-tenths and all-of-book sensitivity in prose with the resulting target at each level, and names what evidence would move the discount: ownership percentages, share of profit, a fair value or transaction price, an impairment test, and distributions from the investees.

challenges.challenge: The investment summary still calls the investment line 'a large part but not all' of the distance between target and price. The net bridge credit is about Rp7.1/share of a Rp31.6 gap, about a fifth; the operating DCF and the liquidity discount are the larger part, so the summary overstates the asset contribution.
challenges.answer: Dropped. The summary now states that the credit net of the two working-capital reversals and the net-debt dating is only about an eighth of the distance between target and price, and that the operating business falling short of the price on any perimeter reading is the larger part. The arithmetic is reproducible from the bridge, the share count and the target.

challenges.challenge: The bridge and the EV/EBITDA method use net debt of Rp16.87bn, the 31 December 2025 position. The 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows cash Rp3.47bn against debt Rp18.42bn, so net debt is Rp14.94bn; the model overstates it by Rp1.93bn (about Rp0.24/share) and the report never dates the figure.
challenges.answer: Added a dated bridge item of plus 1.929bn moving net debt to 30 June 2026: cash of 3.472bn against the 1.543bn the pack still carries at 31 December 2025, with bank and lease debt unchanged at 18.416bn. The label carries the date and the financial section now dates both cash figures rather than saying only that the loan is unchanged.

missing_bull_case.note: The strongest bull - the Rp162.45bn asset at book (Rp20/share) and the exclusive Segafredo rollout - is zero-credited or absent from the scenarios. The bull is a generic +15pp growth / +3pp margin shock whose margin leg contradicts its own 33.1% recovery narrative (C3), so the "bull below the price" conclusion is untested.

missing_bear_case.note: Deconsolidation and an investment write-down - the two risks s5 calls medium likelihood / high impact - are not in the bear, which shocks only growth and margin. The 21 Dec 2026 FTSE review is untested. A 25% bear weight on a two-shock case understates the downside the report itself describes.

assumption_realism.note: The value drivers are the fish spread, the revenue level and terminal cash conversion. Revenue extrapolates the highest half in the file with no mean reversion against the 42% FY2024 fall; the basis compares a six-month fish figure with a twelve-month one; terminal capex is 58% of D&A. The margin path itself reproduces H1 (credit).

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in sources: fish revenue/cogs Rp29.64/19.82bn (33.1%) and Rp45.11/40.28bn (10.7%) [S6 p.86, S5 note 27]; H1 EBIT Rp2.19bn and depreciation Rp5.26bn, a 14.2% margin [S5 p.8]; inventory KAM and management's nil obsolescence provision [S4 p.5, note 7]; airport outlet pipeline [S6 p.4, p.105]; Goldman 45.74% and public 35.33% [S5 note 25]. Wrong: the accruals-ratio claim (C6) and the 27.2x multiple (C9).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF primary is right for the industry and the ten-year fade is appropriate, but first-year FCFF is 90% a non-cash reclassification while the asset that absorbed it is excluded (C1); the treatment is not applied consistently (C2); the multiple uses a branded-manufacturer median on FY2025A EBITDA (C7); terminal capex is below D&A (C8). The WACC sits in the house band but the report omits the 1.62pp spread the engine deducts from rf, so its stated inputs do not reproduce 12.1%.

bias_and_tone.note: "Far outside any acceptable band" and "the whole distance" are not supported by the arithmetic, and a DCF the report itself calls an "upper bound" carries 60% weight. The direction is evidence-led, but the target is pushed up by the two optimistic treatments (phantom cash, peak revenue) while the bull is understated. Every treatment still leaves value below Rp52, so the SELL survives a doubled bear.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right variables: soymeal and wheat rather than the F&B default CPO, cost currency IDR, no royalty regime for F&B, and it deliberately keeps the deck links small (10%/3% of COGS). The deck's FY2027E soymeal/wheat values are used one year early, but the effect is under 2pp of gross margin, so no material inconsistency.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative without a source: the Rp162.45bn investment zero-credited though it is 44% of assets and was contributed at book (defensible only if worthless, which is not shown), and the bull margin +3pp against a 33.1% narrative. Justified: terminal growth 4% (below the 7.04% industry rate, with the share-loss record), payout 0%, capex 7% above the historic nil (deferred maintenance). Shocks are exactly mirrored (+/-15pp growth, +/-3pp margin), so no asymmetry there, but the narratives are asymmetric.

calibration.note: QC has no blocking flags. The -21.2pp EBITDA-margin gap is the disclosed mix shift and the justification cites the segment note that says it [S6 p.86, S5 note 27]. The extreme-call justification names three sourced drivers. The weights.changed WARN is explained in method_note. Calibration passes on margin; FY+1 cash flow, not margin, is the problem (C1).

signoff.notes: APPROVED. SELL, target Rp14 against Rp72. All eleven red-team challenges (C1-C11) and all four sign-off concerns (L1-L4) are answered on substance, and the answers are visible in the current model and prose: one DCF at 100% with EV/EBITDA dropped rather than run through the same bridge twice; the Rp162.45bn investment on the bridge at 70% of book with an explicit 25% write-down probability charged in every scenario (net bridge credit Rp24.6bn); both working-capital releases reversed in the bridge; net debt dated to 30 June 2026 (Rp14.94bn, QC-recomputed); terminal capex at the D&A ratio; and the accruals-ratio claim replaced by the computed 0.9 percent. QC PASS, facts PASS, lint PASS. The target reproduces from the printed numbers: 0.5 x Rp13.41 + 0.25 x Rp10.83 + 0.25 x Rp24.64 = Rp15.6, less the 10 percent liquidity discount = Rp14. The call survives every branch of the credit range: zero credit leaves roughly Rp1-5 a share, full book about Rp22-24, and the reconsolidation bull Rp25, all far below Rp72, so no single judgement produces the rating. Four defects are waived as non-conclusion-changing, none of which moves the target, the rating or a printed number. (1) QC Q1 (FIX, unanswered). s3, s5 and s6 say the stake is classified at fair value through OCI [S5 note 3] as though the filing discloses it. I checked the archive: note 3 is the generic policy only and note 14 carries the three entities and amounts with no designation, so the classification is inferred. That weakens one of the three legs the perimeter reading rests on, but the other two (the balance-sheet arithmetic that the falls sum to the new line, and the nil consideration) stand alone, the report already tells the reader the filing does not settle ownership and that note 1d contradicts it, and it carries both the deconsolidated and the reconsolidated values. A reader reaches the same conclusion about the stock. Correct at the next edit to say we infer FVOCI from the note 3 policy and the absence of equity-accounted income, which is the remedy QC asked for. (2) The COE build-up in s4 prints rf 7.4 percent, ERP 4.2 percent, CRP 2.5 percent and beta 0.92, which sum to 13.6 percent, not the 12.0 percent used: the engine deducts a 1.62pp default spread from rf and the prose omits it (the red team noted this in its checklist). The rate actually applied is 12.0 percent COE / 11.9 percent WACC, inside the IDR 11-13 percent band, so the band claim is true of the model; the printed inputs are simply not reproducible. One line fixes it. (3) Q2 (percentages for the related-party flows) is only half done: s6 gives total assets and revenue in rupiah rather than 1.0 percent and 8.2 percent. Q3 (the capex basis calls 52.7 percent a match for D&A at 50.0 percent) and Q4 (the two bridge reversals held at base-scenario amounts, under Rp0.1/share, directionally against the bear) are NOTE-grade and are described as such. (4) s3 calls the investing cash flow nil; the filing shows Rp112.5m used. Immaterial in size, wrong as a word, and it does not change the no-consideration point. Weighed against a last review round that would park a robust SELL for a three-word citation correction, none of these changes what a reader would conclude about the rating or the price, so they are recorded here rather than returned. The SELL is also not a shared-input tilt: this is the only name at sign-off, the industry is not one-sided (ADES HOLD, six BUYs, STRK SELL), and the 40x trailing EV/EBITDA on negative operating cash flow and an undisclosed 44-percent-of-assets line is name-specific.

bias.note: Base is the most probable path, not the cautious one: FY2026E is the H1 2026 actual (op profit Rp2.19bn + D&A Rp5.26bn = 14.2% EBITDA margin on Rp52.45bn) plus an H2 estate at the level the half printed, FY2027E is the estate annualised and grown 8% (Rp15.87bn), and the 77.0% measured estate margin is held with no haircut. Departures are sourced or disclosed: capex to a maintenance rate (nil actual capex is not sustainable), terminal growth 4% (share loss argued [S7, S8]), and the 30% valuation haircut plus 25% write-down on the credit, which are labelled house judgements with a full range in s4. The SELL survives the whole range: at full book credit the target is about Rp24 and at zero credit about Rp5, both below Rp72, so no unsupported conservatism produces the rating. Scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers with a 50% base.

findings.finding: The investment line is described three times (s5, s6) as classified at fair value through other comprehensive income [S5 note 3, note 14]. Note 3 is the generic FVOCI policy; the archived note 14 shows the three entities and the Rp162.45bn carrying amounts but no statement designating the line at FVOCI. The classification is inferred, not disclosed.

Related-party flows are now itemised in absolute rupiah (receivable Rp3.539bn, land title, investment line) but still not expressed against revenue or assets: the receivable is 8.2% of FY2025 revenue and 1.0% of total assets, and the investment line is 44% of total assets. The method card output contract asks for the percentage.

The capex_pct basis says the terminal 52.7% ratio matches D&A, but terminal capex is Rp12.82bn against D&A of Rp12.16bn (52.7% vs 50.0% of revenue). The report prose is consistent; the assumptions basis line overstates the match.

The two FY2026E/FY2027E working-capital reversals in the bridge are fixed at the base-scenario amounts (Rp-59.541bn and Rp-3.075bn) when the bear and bull are re-run, while their different revenue paths imply about Rp-60.0bn and Rp-59.1bn in FY2026E. The error is under Rp0.1/share and directionally penalises the bear, so it does not distort the call.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -16.2pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2026E is a transition year across two perimeters and no single margin describes it: six months of the fish book at the 10.7% gross margin it printed (Rp45.11bn of Rp52.45bn revenue) and six months of the estate at 77.0% [S5 p.8, note 27]. The group printed an H1 2026 EBITDA margin of 14.2% - operating profit of Rp2.19bn plus depreciation of Rp5.26bn on Rp52.45bn of revenue [S5 p.8] - and the model's FY2026E EBITDA margin is 18.78%, i.e. that half-year run-rate with an estate-only, higher-margin second half. From FY2027E the estate prints 57.5% EBITDA versus FY2025A 35.0% because the low-margin revenue left, not because anything improved. The calibration gap is the perimeter the LK itself created at 30 June 2026 (Rp162.45bn investment against nil), not a price or cost assumption [S5 note 14].

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves +50.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The +50pt move from 27.0% to 77.0% is one event, not a trend: the fish trading book that earned a 10.7% gross margin left the consolidation on 30 June 2026 and the estate that remains earned 77.0% in H1 2026 (F&B, rooms and other revenue against a fraction of that revenue in cost of revenue) [S5 note 27, note 14]. There is no margin assumption inside the drift - FY2027E is the measured estate margin held flat, with no recovery to the FY2025 45.4% group margin.

flags.message: a.opex_pct moves +40.7pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The move from 25.3% to 66.0% is the stranded cost base: the property stayed with the group (the assets that left were Rp65.9bn of construction in progress and Rp60.9bn of inventory inside the Rp162.45bn investment) while the revenue used as the denominator fell to the estate perimeter [S5 note 14, note 1d]. Depreciation of Rp10.53bn on estate revenue of Rp15.87bn is 66.4% on its own; the ratio then falls to 66.0% by FY2035E only because revenue grows over a cost base growing 2% [S4 p.53]. The 68.9% figure is the FY2030E ratio, not the end of the forecast.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves +49.7pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex is brought from the nil actually spent in FY2024, FY2025 and H1 2026 up to the D&A ratio so the perpetuity replaces what it depreciates: gross property of Rp294bn against a Rp10.45bn charge implies a 28-year average life and a replacement run-rate near the charge itself [S4 p.53, S4 p.15, S5 p.11]. The percentage is high only because the revenue denominator lost the trading book; in absolute terms capex rises from Rp1.8bn to Rp12.8bn by FY2035E. A lower terminal capex would manufacture value.

flags.message: expected return -81%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers, all arithmetic from the LK. One: the 30 June 2026 transfer moved Rp162.45bn of assets into an investment line with no ownership or earnings disclosure, so the revenue available to the group falls to the estate perimeter and the investment is carried at a 70%-of-book valuation haircut and a 75% chance of no write-down in the bridge [S5 note 14]. Two: the property kept with the group depreciates Rp10.53bn a year against Rp15.87bn of first-full-year estate revenue, so EBIT is negative once the estate's cash cost is charged and the operating business is worth little more than its maintenance capex profile [S4 p.53, S5 note 30]. Three: operating cash flow has been negative in every year FY2022A-FY2025A (Rp-1.31bn in FY2025 on Rp2.14bn of reported profit) [S4 p.15]. The reverse DCF and the implied exit multiple are reported in s4.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.1}
flags.justification: Only the DCF is weighted, at 100%. EV/EBITDA is dropped because on this name the engine's multiple leg cannot be put on one perimeter: it would apply a peer multiple to trailing FY2025A EBITDA that still contains the fish book which left at 30 June 2026 [S5 note 14], and it shares the DCF's bridge, whose two working-capital reversals exist only inside the DCF's forecast, so the leg would be debited for cash it never received. P/E fails on a profit base under 1% of revenue and a tax rate that ran from 36.2% to nil in two years [S4 p.12, S5 p.8]. Cross-checks are shown unweighted in s4.
